checks.invariant: disk_low() (service.py:282, 388-404) keeps an agent from growing the shared SQLite file past AGENTBOX_MIN_FREE: once the guard admits a call, the call's own writes must be small relative to the margin.
checks.result: Fails. The guard is a single pre-check; the REQUIRE_APPROVAL branch then writes a pending approvals row whose preview is unbounded and amplified. preview_command (preview.py:122-125) appends one ~90-byte Korean note per unrecognised segment, so the 2-byte segment 'x;' yields a 45x larger preview, and approvals.create (approvals.py:53-57) stores args and preview raw. In the sandbox, with min_free_bytes set to free-1MiB (disk_low False), ONE agent call_tool('exec', {'command': 'x;'*65536}) (131097-byte JSON body, default policy exec-needs-approval) returned 202, grew agentbox.db from 4096 to 6004736 bytes plus a 6089392-byte -wal file (WAL mode set at audit.py:260), and disk_low() was True afterwards. The pending row held args 131087 bytes and preview 5832767 bytes (65536 notes). The audit approval_requested row was capped at 83141 bytes by bound_payload, so the growth is in the approvals table only. The ratio is linear, so a body at the 8 MiB AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY cap gives about 366 MiB of DB plus a similar WAL in one admitted call. That one call already exceeds the 256 MiB default margin, and 4 concurrent calls per sandbox (tool_concurrency) all pass the pre-check.

checks.invariant: No other agent-token route or background path writes agent-sized data to SQLite while disk_low is true.
checks.result: Holds apart from the candidate above. Agent-token routes: POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools goes through call_tool and is refused with 507 before close_idle (service.py:282-285). POST /approvals/{aid} skips the approval_forbidden row while low (api.py:312-317). GET /approvals/{aid} (api.py:288-299) runs expire_stale, which only expires or compacts existing rows (at most 20 pending per sandbox) and runs close_idle. close_idle writes one gui_changes or close record per open burst through log_best_effort, and AuditLog.append bounds each payload to 128 KiB (audit.py bound_payload). No new bursts open while low, because agent GUI input is refused. GET /sandboxes/{sid} and GET /sandboxes/{sid}/desktop/state (desktop.py:210) are reads. Unauthenticated or invalid agent tokens do not write audit rows (api.py:173-182).

checks.invariant: Finished-row compaction keeps what the approval card and audit need, and the human can still decide while low.
checks.result: Compaction keeps what the card needs. _finish (service.py:406-411) stores _logged_args (size, sha256, 16 KiB args_head) and bound_payload(preview), and the done list in _approvals.html:26 reads args.command, args.path or args.args_head. The audit row carries the same _logged_args shape. Compaction does not reclaim space: in the local run, expiring the 5.8 MB row raised agentbox.db from 6004736 to 12054528 bytes with 2890 free pages, and nothing in agentbox/ runs VACUUM. Recovery under real pressure therefore needs more free space first. In decide, only claim is wrapped for sqlite3.Error (service.py:446-449). A sqlite3.Error from _finish on the deny path (service.py:462) or after a successful run (service.py:481) propagates as a 500 after the tool has already run, and can leave the row in 'approved'. retention._DONE never prunes 'approved' rows and expire_stale never expires them. Recorded as hardening. While a pending row from the candidate exists, the human approval fragment renders every note (_approvals.html:16, web.py:233). One 128 KiB-body request produced a 7472223-byte HTML fragment, so the UI decision path degrades in proportion. The JSON decide API stays usable.

checks.invariant: The guard measures the filesystem that agent-driven writes land on.
checks.result: disk_low checks shutil.disk_usage(db_path.parent) (service.py:395), and AGENTBOX_DB may differ from AGENTBOX_HOME (config.py:29, 95-96). Approval capture PNGs go to home/captures (api.py:154), which is bounded by the pending cap. docker commit snapshots and the container writable layer land on the Docker data root. They are bounded only by snapshot_quota and the optional AGENTBOX_DISK storage_opt (sandbox.py:263-264), which README:286,360 documents as a partial SB-5 control. While low, every agent call is refused, so no new agent-triggered commits occur. A filesystem mismatch weakens the guard but does not open a separate agent route; recorded as hardening.

checks.invariant: Prior run-4 record agentbox/service.py:_logged_args:tool-args-persisted-to-audit-without-size-cap: agent input reaches the append-only audit log only in bounded form.
checks.result: No longer holds; the root cause is fixed. AuditLog.append applies bound_payload(self._mask(payload)) to every record, so approval previews and str(e) error strings are bounded too. Locally, the approval_requested payload for a 5832767-byte preview was stored as 83141 bytes, and tool_request as 16543 bytes. The masking pass runs before bounding (linear: about 1.0 s for 65536 notes), which is CPU only.

checks.invariant: Pending approvals rows have a per-row size bound in proportion to the request.
checks.result: Fails; this is the same root cause as the disk-guard candidate. approvals.create (approvals.py:49-59) json.dumps raw args and preview, and _call_tool (service.py:332-339) passes the uncapped preview. The 'preview failed' fallback (service.py:334) also copies the raw command. Measured: a 131097-byte request produced a pending row with a 5832767-byte preview (65536 notes). Compaction happens only at finish (service.py:406-411).

checks.invariant: Unmasked approvals data reaches no principal lower than the human.
checks.result: Holds. GET /approvals is human_only (api.py:282-286). GET /approvals/{aid} returns only id, status, result and decided_at to an agent, and only for its own sandbox (api.py:294-298). result is the agent's own tool output. The UI routes need a full-scope human session. approvals rows (args head, preview, result) are not passed through AuditLog._mask, and retention._write_archive (retention.py:67-84) copies them unmasked into the prune archive next to the masked audit rows. The only readers are the human and the host operator, who already hold those values, so this is recorded as hardening rather than a finding.

checks.invariant: Approval rows and side artifacts of a deleted sandbox cannot be acted on or re-executed after deletion, and retention removes finished rows.
checks.result: Holds. delete_sandbox (service.py:538-543) drops capture PNGs, and SandboxManager.delete marks the sandbox deleted (sandbox.py:320-326). Leftover pending rows expire through expire_stale and are compacted. Approving one reaches _snapshot, and sandboxes._container raises SandboxError for a deleted sandbox (sandbox.py:225-228), so decide records FAILED and runs nothing. Finished rows (denied, executed, failed, expired) are removed only by the host prune command (retention.py:41, 54-64), which matches the documented design. The one exception is a row stuck in 'approved' after a _finish storage error (see the unit-1 hardening note).

candidates.title: One agent exec call writes a pending approval row about 45x its body size, getting past the PR #20 disk guard in a single step
candidates.description: PR #20 added AgentBox.disk_low(), a free-space pre-check at the top of call_tool, and compaction of finished approval rows. Pending approval rows are still written raw and without a size bound, and the preview the system computes is amplified from the agent's command. preview_command emits one fixed ~90-byte Korean note for every shell segment it cannot classify, so a command made of 2-byte 'x;' segments (default policy: exec-needs-approval) gives a preview about 45x the request. approvals.create stores that preview plus the raw args in the shared SQLite file, which is in WAL mode, so the data is written twice on disk. The guard was evaluated once before the call and admitted it. Locally, one 131097-byte agent request, made with 1 MiB of headroom above min_free_bytes, added 6.0 MB to agentbox.db and 6.1 MB to the -wal file, and disk_low() flipped to True afterwards. At the 8 MiB body cap the same call writes about 366 MiB of row data plus WAL, which exceeds the 256 MiB default margin on its own. Each sandbox can run 4 such calls concurrently and keep up to 20 pending. Expiry compaction does not shrink the file: it grew from 6.0 to 12.1 MB. Once the volume fills, human writes fail closed (log_human 503, decide claim 503, expire_stale stops), and the human approval UI renders every note of every pending row. This is the part of the run-4 N2 root cause (agent-grown approval rows without an effective aggregate bound) that the PR #20 fix did not cover.
candidates.root_cause: The disk guard is only a threshold check at call entry (service.py:282). The REQUIRE_APPROVAL branch then calls _preview, and preview_command appends one note per unrecognised segment with no count bound (preview.py:122-125); the 200-item cap at preview.py:126 applies only to 'affected'. approvals.create (approvals.py:53-57) stores json.dumps(args) and json.dumps(preview) unbounded. bound_payload is applied only to the audit copy (audit.py append) and to finished rows (_finish, service.py:406-411), never at creation.
candidates.intended_behavior: No single agent request can make the control plane persist more than a small, fixed bound of approval data. Pending rows hold the same bounded shape as the audit log (capped args and capped preview with a bounded notes list), so the 256 MiB guard margin cannot be crossed by an admitted call.

trace.description: An agent token posts {"args": {"command": "x;x;..."}}. _BodyLimit allows up to AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY (8 MiB).
disk_low() is evaluated once. Free space is still above min_free_bytes, so the call is admitted.
policy.decide returns exec-needs-approval because 'x' is not in the read-only allowlist (default_policy.yaml).
_preview calls sandboxes.preview, which calls preview_command, for the raw command.
One note per segment is appended without a bound: 65536 notes for 65536 'x;' segments.
json.dumps(args) and json.dumps(preview) are inserted raw into the shared SQLite file (WAL).

evidence.description: notes.append(f"'{_short_seg(seg)}' 부분의 영향은 ...") runs once per segment. Only 'affected' is truncated, at line 126.
create stores args and preview with json.dumps and no size check.
The only disk guard is a pre-check at call entry.
approvals.create is called with the uncapped preview after the guard.
The shared DB is put in WAL mode, so the large insert is also written to agentbox.db-wal.
The human approval card renders every note of every pending row.

conditions.description: Requires an agent token for a running sandbox. This is the lowest-trust principal, and the threat model assumes it may be prompt-injected.
Default policy (or any policy that sends an exec to require_approval) and AGENTBOX_MIN_FREE > 0. The body must fit AGENTBOX_MAX_BODY (8 MiB default).
Fewer than PENDING_APPROVALS_MAX (20) pending approvals for the sandbox, and free space above min_free_bytes when the call starts.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent holding only its own sandbox's agent token calls the exec tool with a long command made of trivial unrecognised segments.
payloads: POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/exec  {"args": {"command": "x;" * 65536}}  (131097-byte JSON body; scale to ~8 MiB for the deployed cap)
instructions: In tools/sbx (no network, no Docker, 512 MiB, 120 s), build AgentBox with the real AuditLog, ApprovalStore, DesktopControl and default_policy.yaml, plus a fake SandboxManager whose preview() calls the real preview_command with empty glob/walk callbacks (scratch/h.py).
Set settings.min_free_bytes = shutil.disk_usage(home).free - 1 MiB so that disk_low() is False.

Call box.call_tool('sb_x', 'exec', {'command': 'x;'*65536}, actor='agent') once, then measure agentbox.db and agentbox.db-wal, the approvals row lengths, disk_low(), the audit row sizes, the rendered _approvals.html size, and the file size after expire_stale compaction.
execution.observed_result: decision=exec-needs-approval; call_tool status=202; disk_low before=False, after=True; agentbox.db 4096 -> 6004736 bytes (45.8x the body), -wal 6089392 bytes; pending row args 131087 bytes, preview 5832767 bytes, 65536 notes; audit approval_requested payload only 83141 bytes; _approvals.html fragment 7472223 bytes for this one row; after expiry, row compacted to 16533/83045 bytes but agentbox.db grew to 12054528 bytes (2890 free pages); audit verify ok. (agents/h-approvals/artifacts/h.out)

remediation.strategy: Bound pending rows at creation. (1) Reject agent exec commands, and other string args, above a fixed size (for example LOGGED_ARGS_MAX) with 413 before policy and preview. (2) In preview_command, cap the notes (for example, keep the first 50 plus one 'and N more segments' summary). (3) Store bound_payload(preview) in approvals.create. (4) Re-check disk_low() immediately before approvals.create, and treat a sqlite3.Error from create or _finish as 503. (5) Optionally run 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)' and VACUUM after prune, so that compaction and prune actually return space.

code_changes.fixed_code:

                raise ServiceError(507, "컨트롤 플레인 디스크의 남은 공간이 부족해 승인 요청을 만들지 않음.")

likelihood.reason: Any agent token can do it with one ordinary-looking request under the default policy. The threat model assumes a prompt-injected agent.

impact.reason: Shared control-plane disk and availability: a few requests fill the DB volume past the guard, after which human audit-logged actions (decide, delete, pause) fail closed with 503 and the approval UI bloats. Recovery needs the operator to free disk out of band. No integrity or confidentiality loss.

confidence.reason: The full call_tool path ran with the real policy, preview, store and audit code and the observed byte counts. Scaling to the 8 MiB cap is linear arithmetic from the measured 45.8x ratio; filling a real disk was deliberately not tested.

hardening: decide wraps only claim in sqlite3.Error handling. A sqlite3.Error from _finish on the deny path (service.py:462) or after a successful run (service.py:481) returns 500 and can leave a row in 'approved'. retention._DONE never prunes that status and expire_stale never expires it. Catch sqlite3.Error around _finish and retry compaction later.
Approval compaction and prune do not return space: there is no VACUUM or wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) anywhere in agentbox/. Expiring a 5.8 MB row grew agentbox.db from 6.0 to 12.1 MB locally.

disk_low measures db_path.parent only. When AGENTBOX_DB is on a different filesystem from AGENTBOX_HOME (captures) or the Docker data root (snapshots, writable layers), agent-driven growth there is not part of the guard.

approvals rows (args head, preview, result) bypass AuditLog._mask, and retention._write_archive copies them unmasked into the prune archive next to masked audit rows. Readers are human or operator only, but archives may be handed on; mask before compaction or archiving.
AuditLog.append runs _mask over the full unbounded payload before bound_payload (linear, about 1 s for 65536 notes). Bounding first would cap that CPU.

uncovered.surface: POST /sandboxes/{sid}/tools/exec with a long command: Policy.decide (command_names/_words/_raw_hits/simple_programs shlex passes) and preview_command, run on the tool_pool thread before any approval exists
uncovered.boundary: Agent -> control-plane availability: CPU-bound pure-Python policy and preview parsing of an up-to-8 MiB command holds the GIL, which the event loop and human request threads share. Measured locally: Policy.decide took 4.96 s for a 128 KiB 'x;' command and grows at least linearly, so about 5 minutes for a full 8 MiB body, with 4 concurrent per sandbox.
uncovered.reason: No assigned unit owns command-length CPU cost in the policy gate. It needs its own bounded measurement of GIL starvation of the human API and a check of whether a per-command length cap belongs before policy.decide.
